title: Non-cubic (triclinic) simulation box
purpose: Exercises the general-cell code of the `epsr` engine [@soper1996,@soper2005]: a 9-number `.ato` header (nmol and temperature, a b c, and the angles phib thetac phic) instead of the cubic one, so the minimum-image convention, the cell neighbour lists and the density use a non-orthogonal metric. Needed for crystalline or anisotropic boxes [@epsrmanual].
system: The EPSR-test system: a liquid mixture of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO, (CH3)2SO) and 400 water molecules (DMSO mole fraction 1/3; 3200 atoms) at 300 K, here in a triclinic cell with a = b = c = 33.1213 Å, b at phib = 80° from a in the xy plane, and c tilted by thetac = 10° from z at azimuth phic = 20° (EPSR's cell convention). The cell volume, a·b·c·sin(phib)·cos(thetac) ≈ 35240 Å³, gives an atomic number density of 0.0908 atoms/Å³ (0.0881 in the cubic box). DMSO uses EPSR's Lennard-Jones + Coulomb reference potential with methyl rotational groups; water uses SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charge parameters [@berendsen1987] with EPSR's flexible intramolecular geometry (O-H 0.976 Å). The empirical potential is refined against three neutron diffraction data sets of deuterated DMSO in D2O, in null-scattering H2O/D2O and in H2O (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), the isotope-substitution approach of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992].
inputs: Copy of EPSR-test with only the first line of the `.ato` replaced by the three-line general-cell header `600 300.0` / `33.1213 33.1213 33.1213` / `80.0 10.0 20.0`; the molecular coordinates are unchanged.
verification: Two chained passes, the second reading the 9-number header written by `moloutc`. Evidence that the general-cell branch is active: the `.out` of the Fortran reference reports number density 0.90808E-01 (cubic EPSR-test: 0.88070E-01), and the written `.ato` keeps the three-line cell header. All 27 output files are identical after both passes.
